summary: Iteration 98 was the final retest of FIX A to E plus the money regression and a frontend spot check. Regression is green: owner_batch 13/13, recharge_and_settlement 16/16, iter96_fixes 11/11, and pytest across iter96_reconciliation, iter97_returns_outstanding, iter97_recharge_notify and iter97_concurrency gave 12 passed and 1 skipped (the 429 rate-limit skip). The new suite tests/test_iter98_final_batch.py gave 6 passed and 1 failed. FIX A holds: parking a ₹250 refund 3 times left Receivables, vendor_receivable and net worth at Δ0 and sent exactly 1 'Refund blocked' nudge. A company-funded refund (₹200, seller had ₹50) raised Receivables by exactly ₹150 with one open row and one refund_company_funded txn, and a replay changed nothing. Net worth stayed at Δ0, which is the correct accounting: +150 receivable, +200 customer-wallet liability, -50 vendor payable. FAIL: the ₹150 company-funded receivable can never be recovered. The admin recover endpoint answers nothing_to_recover while the seller holds ₹500, and the row stays open. FIX B: no open return_refund rows remain, Receivables are 0.0 and the 11 rows the script closed all belonged to completed/paid returns. However, the script reads db.order_returns, a collection that does not exist. FIX C: group_1 platform_fee is 1169.82, which equals the fee rows (4369.82) minus |reversals| (3200). Rows ran 1169.82 → 1297.82 → 1169.82, the replayed reject changed nothing, 276686a3 has exactly one 128 reversal, no reversal amount is negative and no withdrawal has a duplicate reversal. However, 9 earlier rejected settlements kept their ₹128 fee (₹1,152 in total). FIX D: on both the parcel and the recharge order each real move sent exactly 1 buyer and 1 seller notice, and replaying the same status twice sent nothing. Pushes are 📦 for parcel and ⚡ for recharge, with one push per status key. Recharge copy is 'Recharge update' with no 'parcel'. FIX E: DTH plus [airtel, tata-play] saves only tata-play. Excel: the admin group-wise export has 21 sheets including Recharge and no transaction in more than one group sheet or twice in a sheet. Every delivery_charge_paid, withdrawal_hold, withdrawal_transaction_fee, return_refund_debit, cashback_recovery and reversal row sits in the Debit column with a remark. The vendor export's Reconciliation sheet says Balanced: NO, and its lines do not add up. A duplicate scan across 17 ledger types found 0 double entries. Frontend: the admin Shop tab swipes to Payouts, the payouts strip swipes Pending → Processing → Success and stays on /admin/payouts, and the Bag footer shows a live wallet of ₹47,497, the same as /auth/me. No deprecated Expo packages were checked this round (no frontend code changed).

critical.issue: Nothing in the code ever recovers this receivable. core/cashback._settle_outstanding_rows (core/cashback.py:782) only matches kind='cashback', and recover_outstanding_from_wallet uses users.cashback_outstanding. As a result POST /admin/cashback/outstanding/{vendor}/recover returned {applied:0, reason:'nothing_to_recover'} while the seller had ₹500, and the ₹150 row stayed open. The seller is told 'It will be recovered from your next sales', but no sale-credit path does that either. Receivables can only go up for these rows, so the 'recover brings both back down' requirement cannot be met.

minor.issue: The script queries db.order_returns, but the real collection is db.returns and order_returns does not exist. Every lookup returns None, so EVERY open return_refund row is closed as 'missing', including genuinely parked refunds. It got the right result this time only because all 11 returns were already completed/paid. Fix the collection name before anyone re-runs it.

9 testvendor settlements rejected on 2026-10-23 between 05:34 and 05:51 (2e86cd13, e69b6eb1, 60810a9c, 55baa41e, 6e553bf4, 78c837f1, f6774f14, 4b5b651d, 70eed9b8) each have withdrawal_transaction_fee and platform_fee_collected rows of ₹128, but no WDL_FEEBACK refund and no reversal. The seller is short ₹1,152 and platform_fee revenue is ₹1,152 too high. The books are internally consistent, but this breaks the rule that a rejected settlement costs no fee. The backfill skips these because it only reverses when a fee refund already exists. It needs to post both the fee refund and the reversal for them.

routes/vendor_networth.py:140-153 builds the breakdown without the withdrawal_reversals bucket (credit ₹1,83,722), delivery_charge_reversals (₹30) or cashback_funding_returned. The lines shown for testvendor sum to -1,69,973.5, while '= Ledger balance' says 13,778.5, so the owner cannot tie the sheet.

The stored vendor_earnings is 7,062.5 against a ledger of 13,778.5, a gap of -6,716 (Balanced: NO). RCA: there are 92 places where a row's previous_balance does not match the previous row's new_balance. Most are round-number jumps (to 9000, 10000, 20000) left by test fixtures that $set vendor_earnings directly. Since 2026-10-20 the net jump is only ₹14. Consider posting a single vendor_adjustment row to re-baseline the CI vendor.

The kind 'delivery_fee_company_funded' is never written anywhere, so that filter is dead. Open 'delivery_fee' rows (a seller short on the delivery fee he owes us, created at core/shop_money.py:508) are now left out of Receivables, so money owed to Slangcart would show up nowhere. There are 0 open rows today.
Operators are filtered only when at least one kind is ticked. kinds:[] with networks:['airtel','tata-play'] persists both mobile and DTH operators (routes/delivery_partner.py:427).
The seller notice body for a recharge reads 'RC-xxx is now shipped' / 'out for delivery', which is parcel wording.
3 legacy cashback_vendor_recovery rows (TXNA208, TXNA1295, TXNA1514, UPI deposits of ₹30/₹30/₹40) appear as Credits in the Vendor Wallet sheet, although they never touched the vendor wallet.

issues: The hint 'Add ₹99,900 more to your bag to get free delivery' implies a ₹1,00,000 free-delivery threshold. Please check the setting.

Fix scripts/close_stale_parked_refunds.py so it reads db.returns, not db.order_returns.
Post the missing fee refund (WDL_FEEBACK) and the keyed fee reversal for the 9 rejected settlements listed. That is ₹1,152 back to testvendor and off platform_fee revenue.
Add the withdrawal_reversals, delivery_charge_reversals and cashback_funding_returned lines to the vendor net-worth breakdown and the Reconciliation sheet so the lines sum to the ledger balance.
Decide whether open 'delivery_fee' rows are a receivable. Remove the dead 'delivery_fee_company_funded' kind or actually write it.
Optional: drop mobile operators when no kind is ticked, and use recharge wording in the seller's status notice.
critical_code_review_comments: In core/returns.py the company-funded branch calls credit_admin_bucket('shopping_margin', -x). That call is a no-op, because the bucket is owner-locked at server.py:6824, so it is harmless but misleading.
routes/withdrawals.py:372: vendor 'outstanding' sums every open vendor_outstanding kind, including parked return_refund rows. Those are owed to the customer, not to Slangcart.

rca_of_issue: Company-funded receivable: core/returns.py writes kind 'return_refund_company_funded', but the only recovery code (core/cashback._settle_outstanding_rows and recover_outstanding_from_wallet) matches kind 'cashback' and users.cashback_outstanding. To reproduce: seed a vendor with ₹50 and a ₹200 return, POST /refund (409), then POST /refund-from-company. Give the vendor ₹500 and POST /admin/cashback/outstanding/{vid}/recover: the response is nothing_to_recover and the row stays open.
